english: In a triangle $ABC$, let $a,b,c$ denote the lengths of the sides opposite to the angles $A,B,C$, respectively. The incircle of the triangle has radius $2$ and touches the side $AB$ at the point $F$ with $AF=3$. If the area of the triangle $ABC$ is $24$, then the value of $a^2-b^2-c^2$ is ______.
hindi: एक त्रिभुज $ABC$ में माना $a,b,c$ क्रमशः कोणों $A,B,C$ की सम्मुख भुजाओं की लम्बाइयाँ हैं। त्रिभुज के अन्तःवृत्त की त्रिज्या $2$ है तथा यह भुजा $AB$ को बिन्दु $F$ पर स्पर्श करता है, जहाँ $AF=3$ है। यदि त्रिभुज $ABC$ का क्षेत्रफल $24$ है, तो $a^2-b^2-c^2$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: The tangent length from $A$ to the incircle is $AF=s-a$, so $s-a=3$.
Sub-multiple angle formulae with $t=\tan\dfrac A2=\dfrac23$: $\cos A=\dfrac{1-t^2}{1+t^2}=\dfrac{5/9}{13/9}=\dfrac5{13}$ and $\sin A=\dfrac{2t}{1+t^2}=\dfrac{4/3}{13/9}=\dfrac{12}{13}$.
Existence: $s=\dfrac{\Delta}{r}=12$, $a=s-3=9$, $b+c=15$, $bc=52$; $b,c$ are the roots of $x^2-15x+52=0$, which are real and positive ($225-208=17>0$), and $a=9<b+c$.
originality_note: New: the angle A is fixed only through the incircle data (radius and tangent length from A), read as tan(A/2) by the half-angle formula; the sub-multiple formulae then give sin A and cos A, and the area gives bc, while b and c themselves stay irrational (way 5: half-angle formula of the triangle and sub-multiple angle formulae). Closest known: 'r = (s - a) tan(A/2)' exercises. Different because: the asked quantity needs only bc and cos A, so the solver must avoid finding the sides.
stem_review: Read as a student: every point, side, angle and symbol is introduced before use, all conditions are stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently in Python (sympy), is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Checked that a triangle with r = 2, AF = 3 and area 24 exists (a = 9, b + c = 15, bc = 52). Changed: No change.
key_step: Reading tan(A/2) = r/(s-a) from the incircle data and converting it to sin A and cos A.
justification: Routine chain of standard formulae (half-angle, t-formulae, area, cosine rule) with no insight; the numerical sign is the only trap. Comparable to 2021-P1-Q18 (L2).

concept_use.Sub-multiple angles and half-angle formu: cos A = (1-t^2)/(1+t^2) and sin A = 2t/(1+t^2) with t = tan(A/2).
